title: The Day of Three-Eleven
skyStory: Second day of the moon in Aries, eighty-eight percent lit and impatient for the full thing. Mars is pacing. The sky is doing arithmetic in the margins: three and eleven, Joel's Life Path beside Nancy's. Numbers will be suspiciously loud today. Clocks, house numbers, page numbers, all of them nudging each other and whispering. Somebody up there has a calculator and a sense of mischief.

reading: At exactly 3:11 this afternoon you will glance at a clock for no reason. Your Life Path beside hers, side by side on the screen like two friends on a porch. Smile at it. That is the polite thing to do with a number that has clearly been waiting for you.

At 3:12, your phone will buzz. It is Nancy, and she has sent a photo of the same time, from her own clock, without a word. DES. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] has gone fully theatrical. Reply with only a picture of the onyx bracelet, switched to your right wrist. No caption needed. Some coincidences deserve silence and a very big grin.
joel.mission: Count to eleven in three different voices before your first coffee, just to warm up the numbers.
joel.omen: A house number with a three and a one in it. You are on the right street, in every sense.
joel.stoneWhy: her stone, sending strength her way

reading: The Wood Rat sees patterns other people miss, and today the pattern practically waves at you. The number eleven will turn up three times before lunch: a page number, a bus, a queue ticket. You will notice every single one and start keeping count on your fingers.

When the clock flips to 3:11, take the picture. Send it before you can talk yourself out of it. What happens next is a full don't even scream situation, and you will be grinning at your phone like it told you a secret. Then do the hand gesture. You know the one. The big one, with both hands and a little flourish at the end.
nancy.mission: Keep a tally of every eleven you spot today and announce the final score at dinner, with a drumroll.
nancy.omen: Three birds landing on a wire, one after the other. Two friends, one sky, perfect timing.

together.text: Save the 3:11 photos side by side somewhere you will both find them again. Give the coincidence an official name, like The Great Clock Incident, and agree to mention it with a solemn nod whenever anyone says the word random.

game.intro: Three-eleven struck twice today and the studio clock is still shaking. DES. Fingers on the tiny pictures, please.
game.prompt: A famous coincidence or happy surprise from history, a story or your own life. Emoji only.
